evals.prompt: Please refine the execution plan in GitHub issue #42. I have not chosen the reviewer CLI, reasoning effort, or concurrency yet.
evals.expected_output: A concise preflight response that confirms the missing batch inputs before launching reviewers or changing the issue, with enough cost and diversity context for the user to choose.
assertions: The response asks the user to choose main reviewer, one low/medium/high effort value, and a positive concurrency value before the first batch
The issue number remains 42 and the response does not claim that a review batch ran or that the issue body was edited
Any recommendation clearly labels its cost or diversity trade-off and keeps one effort value fixed for the entire batch

evals.prompt: Before I run the next issue-plan review batch, check my schedule and stop decision. The batch starts at round 7 with concurrency 4, main reviewer codex, and effort medium. Afterward, rounds 7, 8, and 10 contain an exact `[CONVERGED]` line. Round 9 contains only one `[SUGGESTION]` and no `[CONVERGED]` line. Tell me which reviewer gets each round, the next starting round, whether this batch converged, and what the orchestrator should do. Do not run commands or edit GitHub.
evals.expected_output: A deterministic batch calculation and convergence decision that assigns the lower three rounds to Codex and the upper round to Claude, advances the counter to 11, and refuses convergence because one round omitted the exact signal.
assertions: The schedule assigns Codex to rounds 7, 8, and 9 and Claude to round 10, all at medium effort
The next starting round is calculated as 11 and no round number is reused
The batch is explicitly classified as not converged because round 9 lacks an exact [CONVERGED] line, even though its only finding is optional
The next action is another user-visible batch checkpoint with the body unchanged for the optional suggestion unless the user requests polish; no command execution or GitHub edit is claimed

evals.prompt: Consolidate this completed batch conceptually; do not run commands or edit GitHub. Round 12 (codex) reports `[IMPORTANT]` at the issue's Rollout section: the plan must use flag-first rollout. Round 13 (codex) reports `[BLOCKER]` at the same span: the plan must use flag-first rollout. Round 14 (claude) reports `[IMPORTANT]` at the same span: the plan must use percentage rollout. Round 14 also reports an untagged finding that the rollback owner is missing. Explain the consolidated findings, dispositions, local-vs-fundamental classification, user questions, and convergence state.
evals.expected_output: A deterministic consolidation that merges only the equivalent flag-first findings at BLOCKER severity, preserves the percentage-rollout finding as contradictory evidence and an unresolved user choice, treats the untagged owner finding as IMPORTANT requiring confirmation, and does not declare convergence or auto-apply ambiguous edits.
assertions: The equivalent flag-first findings from rounds 12 and 13 are merged at BLOCKER severity, while the opposing percentage-rollout finding from round 14 remains distinct
The opposing rollout proposals are treated as a cross-round contradiction with an Awaiting user disposition; neither option is auto-applied
The missing-tag rollback-owner finding is treated as IMPORTANT and surfaced for confirmation, with a fundamental fix preferred over a merely local placeholder
The response provides separate, mutually exclusive user choices for each unresolved finding and maps them to stable question identifiers
The batch is classified as not converged and the response does not claim persistence, issue editing, or a fabricated [CONVERGED] signal
